Without a write-ahead log, a database would lose all data written since the last checkpoint.

A write-ahead log allows a database to ensure that all transactions are properly recorded before they are applied to the database. When a transaction is committed, the database writes a record of that transaction to the log before applying the changes to the database. This record includes the transaction's ID, the type of operation, and the data involved. If the database crashes or shuts down, the log remains on disk and can be used to recover the state of the database.

When the database is restarted, it can look at the log and reapply the transactions that were recorded but not yet applied when the crash occurred. This ensures that all data written since the last checkpoint is preserved, even if the database crashed before it could record it. The database can continue where it left off, applying the remaining transactions in the log to ensure a consistent state. This way, the database avoids data loss and can maintain its integrity even after a crash.

The write-ahead log acts as a safety net, protecting the database from data loss in the event of a failure. It allows the database to recover from a crash and continue operating without losing any data that was written but not yet committed. This ensures that the database remains available
